notes: Overall a solid, well-structured implementation. Specific issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION — the Router directly calls `this.taskService.getById(taskId)` and `this.userService.getById(authorId)` inside the POST /comments handler to resolve task title, author name, and assigneeId before forwarding them to CommentService.create(). This means the Router is performing cross-service data resolution, effectively acting as a mediator between services. Rule 1 says no direct service-to-service calls, but the Router doing cross-service lookups to paper over inter-service coupling is a design smell that circumvents the spirit of the rule — the comment.added event payload is enriched with data from other services' stores via the router, rather than services being truly independent. (2) The workaround of passing taskTitle, authorName, and assigneeId as extra parameters to CommentService.create() is an architectural compromise — it leaks TaskService and UserService concerns into the CommentService interface. A cleaner solution would have TaskService publish richer events or have NotificationService query only its own data. (3) Error classification in the router catch block uses brittle string matching on error messages (e.g., checking for 'not found', 'required', 'Invalid JSON') to determine HTTP status codes — this is fragile and error-prone; typed custom error classes would be far more robust. (4) DELETE /projects/:id/members uses a request body, which is non-standard HTTP (DELETE with body is discouraged). (5) No input validation for email format, duplicate email checking, or ensuring assigneeId/userId actually exist in their respective stores before operations. (6) GET /tasks only supports filtering by projectId; there is no way to get all tasks or filter by assignee. (7) The same-level status transition rejection (in-progress → in-progress) is correctly handled because newIndex <= oldIndex covers equality. (8) The demo script is thorough and well-structured with clear assertions. (9) TypeScript types are clean and well-defined throughout. (10) EventBus is simple, correct, and synchronous as required. All six services are in separate files as required.
